rationale: The Prepaid page computes an average per quarter hour; the cited invoice page adds that the digital meter registers every 15 minutes, so per-quarter measurement is supported.
Leefmilieu Brussel requires an EPB periodic inspection every 2 years for a natural-gas boiler; 'minstens' does not change the obligation.
EUR 600 per appliance is the base amount for a heating or combined heat pump in the 2025-2026 regime table. Currency is handled separately by the deadline check.
EUR 280 per appliance is the base amount for a domestic-hot-water-only heat pump in the 2025-2026 regime table. Currency is handled separately by the deadline check.
Vlaanderen.be advises contacting the supplier to discuss adjusting the advance; the answer restates this faithfully for Flanders.
20,957 c/kWh excl. VAT is the Q4 2026 total for the exclusive-night meter, the low end of the stated range.
25,331 c/kWh excl. VAT is the Q4 2026 total for single-rate and for the day register of dual-rate meters, the high end of the stated range; the dual-rate night value 24,208 lies inside it.
5,738 c/kWh excl. VAT is the Q4 2026 social tariff total for natural gas (and heat).
Prepaid page: part of the network costs is billed on the (monthly) peak, and that is the capacity tariff.
Invoice page advises using as few appliances as possible within the same quarter hour.
The digital meter registers consumption every 15 minutes and reports the average power per quarter.
Month peak is defined as the highest quarter-hour power in the month.

The average month peak over the preceding 12 months is the value used to compute the capacity tariff. The page also defines a billing peak (weighted average over the settlement period) that the answer omits; acceptable simplification.
The only passage is an explicitly indicative Prepaid example (EUR 40 per kW/year). It is consistent with a per-kW tariff but is not a rule statement for regular customers.

The 'always at least 2.5 kW' passage sits under Prepaid customers, and the other 2.5 kW passages concern classic meters. The answer puts the minimum under digital meters; the fetched pages do not state it for regular digital-meter customers.
The classic meter cannot measure peaks, so Fluvius works with an average peak of 2.5 kW.
For classic meters, a larger share of network costs is still based on consumption.
Classic meter: a fixed amount based on a minimum peak of 2.5 kW, plus a higher consumption-based charge.
Follows from the definition of the quarter peak as average power per quarter hour; the 'seconds' illustration is an inference, not a quote.
General advice consistent with limiting consumption per quarter hour; the appliance list is illustrative.
The cited professional page: every 2 years for gas boilers and water heaters in the Brussels-Capital Region.
The periodic EPB inspection must be done by a certified EPB boiler technician; the answer shortens the title.
An inspection is also required after repairs to the combustion part, e.g. replacing or adjusting the burner.
The 2025-2026 Prime Habitation lists heat pumps, but applications closed on 30 September 2026; 'bestaat' in the present tense is misleading on 13 October 2026.

The page describes a temporary 2025-2026 regime whose applications, including final invoices, had to be submitted by 30 September 2026. Calling it the current regime on 13 October 2026 is contradicted.
The base amount can be multiplied by 2, 3, 4 or 6 depending on income and household composition.
The 01/01/26 date heads the income-threshold table, not a change in the multipliers, which apply to the whole regime. The answer misattributes the date.
The page lists conditions on the applicant, the building and the works; the answer's 'woning, werken en installatie' is a fair summary.
The prime is capped at 70% (R1-R2) or 50% (R3-R4) of eligible VAT-inclusive invoice items.
BRUGEL states advances are always based on an estimate, but only for Brussels; the answer states it generally without a Flemish or Walloon passage.
Vlaanderen.be: the advance can also be adjusted in the supplier's online customer zone.
BRUGEL explains that the regularisation bill offsets advances against actual consumption, but only for Brussels; the answer generalises to all of Belgium.
BRUGEL says certain suppliers are willing to adjust by agreement; 'doorgaans' (usually) overstates this.
BRUGEL: a supplier that refuses to reduce the advance must justify the refusal.
CREG: the social tariff helps persons or households through a reduced electricity and gas tariff.
Vlaanderen.be confirms it is the same with all suppliers across Belgium; 'ongeacht netbeheerder' is not stated on the fetched pages.
CREG calculates the social tariff every 3 months.
Both CREG Q4 PDFs state the period 1 October 2026 - 31 December 2026.
Separate social tariffs exist for single-rate, dual-rate and exclusive-night meters.
The amounts are excl. VAT, but CREG also excludes the energy contribution, special excise and (in Flanders) the energy fund levy. 'excl. btw' alone suggests an otherwise all-in price.
The amount is excl. VAT, but CREG also excludes the energy contribution, special excise and (in Wallonia) the connection fee. 'excl. btw' alone suggests an otherwise all-in price.
CREG sets the amount and its quarterly calculation, but explicitly does not decide who receives it; 'officiële bron voor de regeling' overstates CREG's role.
Granted only to persons or households receiving certain benefits or allowances.
Eligible categories receive it automatically, with stated exceptions (e.g. category 4), so 'in veel gevallen' is accurate.
CREG refers to the FOD Economie page for conditions and how to apply.

Compensation requires a feed-in contract; without one the surplus is injected for free (Vlaanderen.be). The opening sentence states it unconditionally and the answer never mentions the no-contract case.
The digital meter measures injected electricity exactly; offtake is billed separately.
After the switch, invoice components are charged on actual offtake, i.e. no netting.
Owners with a digital meter can conclude a feed-in contract with their supplier.
VNR notes suppliers sometimes tie the feed-in contract to their own supply contract; its comparison tool exists because terms differ.
VNR only estimates an average compensation for a given injection volume; there is no single fixed amount.
Injected electricity can be sold to the supplier under a feed-in contract.
The VNR estimate depends on the injected volume; contract terms are covered by the comparison guidance.
VNR advises maximising self-consumption during production hours to buy less electricity.
Gas central heating from 20 kW: maintenance every two years.
Maintenance of gas or oil boilers must be done by a certified technician.
Below 20 kW maintenance is not mandatory but recommended.
The power in kW is on the boiler's rating plate.
The page describes Mijn VerbouwPremie for heat pumps and the 2026 amounts.
Amounts depend on type and income category, but the 1 March 2026 change applies to categories 1-2 and non-residential buildings; categories 3-4 have no such date split. The date is misattributed.
Category 3 geothermal: 6.000 euro.
Category 4 geothermal: 8.000 euro.
Category 3 air-water: 4.500 euro.
Category 4 air-water: 6.000 euro.
Category 3 air-air: 450 euro.
Category 4 air-air: 600 euro.
Category 3 hybrid: 3.000 euro.
Category 4 hybrid: 4.000 euro.
Maximum 35% of the invoice (excl. VAT) for category 3; the answer omits 'excl. VAT'.
Maximum 50% of the invoice (excl. VAT) for category 4; the answer omits 'excl. VAT'.
Category 2 amounts from 1 March 2026 are lower (e.g. 4.000 / 1.500 euro).
Category 4 amounts apply to owner-occupiers in category 4 or landlords to a housing company.
The Renolution page describes premium J4 for heating with a heat pump.
Category I air/water: 4.500 EUR per dwelling unit.
Category II air/water: 4.750 EUR per dwelling unit.
Category III air/water: 5.000 EUR per dwelling unit.
Category I water/water or ground/water: 5.800 EUR per dwelling unit.
Category II water/water or ground/water: 6.150 EUR per dwelling unit.
Category III water/water or ground/water: 6.500 EUR per dwelling unit.
For residential buildings the amount varies with the income category.
Non-residential: 35% of eligible invoice costs.
The page names J9 - heat pump boiler (not combinable with J4 for the same installation).
The passage mentions the IRISbox counter for declaring received aid, not as the place to check eligibility before works.
Apply after the works, at the latest 12 months after the final invoice.
The Ombudsman requires prior steps with the company; 'in writing' and keeping the reply are not stated on the fetched federal or Brussels pages.
Steps with the company are required before filing with the Ombudsman.
BRUGEL's dispute service handles unresolved disputes about applying the Brussels electricity and gas ordinances.
The dispute service helps free of charge.
Disputes with suppliers or the DSO Sibelga.
The dispute service's decisions are binding.
The federal Ombudsman handles complaints about the functioning of the electricity and gas market.
Not a tax but a tariff for using the transmission and distribution networks.
Explicitly 'il ne s'agit pas d'une taxe'.
Prosumers with decentralised production such as PV up to 10 kVA.
Capacity/flat-rate and proportional/actual tariffs.
The capacity tariff is in EUR/kWe of net developable power, for customers without a double-flow smart meter.
A standard self-consumption share is assumed. Note the official pages disagree on the figure (SPW 37.76%, ORES 40.26%); the answer gives none.
With a double-flow meter the amount is based on gross kWh actually taken from the grid.
The SPW passage limits the cap statement to the 2020-2023 network tariffs; current validity is not shown.
SPW says the prosumer tariff is CWaPE's competence; publication per distribution operator is not shown because the CWaPE page was blocked.
Dependence on installation power is supported; dependence on location (operator) is not shown on the fetched pages.
Higher self-consumption than the standard share can make the proportional tariff more attractive.
Every three years for small domestic gas boilers.
By a technician certified for gaseous or liquid fuels.
Maintenance is not regulated by Walloon law but recommended.
CREG: consumers can terminate at any time with one month's notice and no termination fee.
SMEs are included on the Brussels BRUGEL page only; the federal CREG passage speaks of consumers. The answer applies it to all of Belgium.
CREG: regardless of fixed-term or indefinite contracts.
